questions.topic: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows
questions.question: What does an SCD Type 2 change create?
options: A new dimension version that leaves the old row in place
An overwrite that replaces the old row's tracked values
A separate fact table for each attribute being tracked
A deletion of the business key once the change is applied

questions.topic: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows
questions.question: Which predicate implements a half-open validity interval?
options: `effective_from <= event_time and event_time <= effective_to`
`effective_from <= event_time and event_time < effective_to`
`effective_from > event_time and event_time >= effective_to`
`effective_from = event_time or event_time = effective_to`

questions.topic: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows
questions.question: Why are half-open intervals useful for adjacent versions?
options: They let the pipeline drop effective timestamps altogether
They let both adjacent rows match an event at the shared boundary
They give exactly one version ownership of a shared boundary
They force a measurable gap between every pair of versions

questions.topic: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows
questions.question: What does an early-binding fact pipeline store?
options: The dimension's current-row flag at the time of loading
The name of the dimension table the fact will join to
The range-join predicate, stored as text on the fact row
The surrogate key of the dimension version that was resolved

questions.topic: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows
questions.question: A region version is valid [Jan 1, Mar 15) and the next is [Mar 15, infinity). Which version matches an event at Mar 15 exactly?
options: The second version
The first version
Both of the versions
Neither of the versions

questions.topic: SCD Type 2: Effective-From and Effective-To Rows
questions.question: Why can a late-arriving historical change require fact restatement in an early-binding model?
options: The dimension table drops its old versions as soon as a new one arrives
Surrogate keys already written on facts may point at the wrong version
A dimension row cannot be inserted once its interval has closed
Late changes must be discarded because intervals are immutable

questions.question: What should remain stable across versions of one logical document?
options: The exact bytes of the document body as stored
The character offsets of every chunk boundary
The document's stable business identifier
The output produced by the current parser version

questions.question: What should identify one immutable state of a document?
options: The current-row flag carried on the latest row
The name of the source collection it came from
The title recorded on the document at ingest
A distinct identifier for that one version

questions.question: How does a content hash reduce false versions during repeated crawls?
options: Identical normalized content always yields the same hash
Hashing prevents metadata and permissions from changing
The hash replaces effective-from and effective-to times
Each crawl is forced to mint a new version identifier

questions.question: Why should chunks belong to a document version rather than only a document ID?
options: Every version of one document produces exactly the same chunk offsets
Changed content shifts boundaries, text, embeddings, and citations
A chunk row cannot store a content hash of its own text
Document versions carry no lineage back to the source bytes

questions.question: A policy is effective July 1 but ingested July 3. Which time answers what the retrieval system could know on July 2?
options: The policy's source-effective time
The effective time of the prior policy
The observation or ingestion time
The release date of the parser version

questions.question: Why can two versions reference the same content blob but still require separate metadata rows?
options: Hashing identical bytes returns a different value each run
Stored blobs cannot be compressed once a version uses them
Two versions of one document always share a validity interval
Permissions, metadata, or effective intervals can still differ

questions.question: What should primarily determine historical retention?
options: Concrete analytical, audit, legal, or reproducibility needs
A standing rule to keep every byte the pipeline ever wrote
The number of dashboards currently reading from the table
Whether the storage tier still has unused capacity left

questions.question: Why is keeping all history indefinitely not automatically safe?
options: It stops auditors from reconstructing what a value once was on a date
It raises cost, breach exposure, discovery scope, and privacy risk
It leaves versioned rows unqueryable by any ordinary SQL engine
It forces every archived copy to be deleted on a fixed schedule

questions.question: Which source is often better modeled as an event fact than as millions of tiny Type 2 intervals?
options: A slowly changing contractual tier
A product's original launch category
A high-frequency telemetry attribute
A customer's current display name

questions.question: What must deletion policy cover besides the primary document row?
options: The catalog entry's table description and column comments
The row-count metrics published on the pipeline dashboard
The business keys shared with the upstream source system
Derived chunks, embeddings, caches, exports, and backups

questions.question: A billing decision depends only on status at midnight each day. Which history grain may be sufficient?
options: One snapshot row per entity per day
Every millisecond-level change, kept forever
One current row carrying no dates at all
A random monthly sample of the entities

questions.question: Which test most directly catches ambiguous temporal truth?
options: Count the columns present in each dimension table
Verify that intervals for one business key never overlap
Check that every stored text value in the table is unique
Require every version of a key to share identical content
